title: In Vain We Thus Recall to Mind
description: In Vain We Thus Recall to Mind in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: William Gaskell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 149, “Following After Jesus”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: In vain we thus re-call to mind The cross our Mas-ter bore, Un-less a holi-er strength we find, And love his spir-it more.

lines: In vain we thus recall to mind
Unless a holier strength we find,
May we, like him, though thanked with ill;
In hope and patience labor still
Like him may we, unmurmuring, go
And learn, 'midst gathering storms of woe,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Gaskell died in 1884.
credits: Words by William Gaskell (1805–1884), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
